### Donor Retention Benchmarks for Nonprofits (2025–2026)

Donor retention rates measure the percentage of last year's donors who give again this year, calculated as (repeat donors / total prior-year donors) × 100. Benchmarks vary by source, donor type (e.g., new vs. repeat), organization size, and data period, but industry averages typically range from **35–55%** overall. Rates are consistently higher for repeat donors and lower for new ones. Here's a synthesis of the most recent data from key reports:

#### Overall Donor Retention Benchmarks
| Source | Year/Period | Overall Rate | Notes |
|--------|-------------|--------------|-------|
| Fundraising Effectiveness Project (FEP) via 4aGoodCause [1] | 2025–2026 | **42.9%** | Average across nonprofits; stable at 40–45% for years. Small nonprofits (<1,000 donors): realistic goal 35–45%. |
| Virtuous Software (771 mid-sized US nonprofits) [2] | 2026 | **54.73%** | Top quartile: 69.64%. Digital-first orgs often hit 53% [5]. |
| Fundraising Report Card [3,7] | 2024–2025 | **~35%** (avg); **53.65%** repeat | Live benchmark; under 35% needs urgent attention. |
| CCS Fundraising [9] | 2025 | **46%** | Internal data analytics average. |
| NPTechForGood [8] | 2024 | **45%** | Down 2.6% from 2023. |
| Bloomerang (FEP Q3) [4] | 2025 | **31.9%** | Slight increase from 31.7% in 2024; quarterly snapshot. |

- **Key Insight**: Most nonprofits retain ~40–50% of donors annually, meaning they lose more than they keep without strong strategies. Top performers (e.g., 55–70%) focus on stewardship, monthly giving (up to 90% retention [1]), and second gifts.

#### Breakdown by Donor Type
| Donor Segment | Average Rate | Source/Notes |
|---------------|--------------|--------------|
| **New Donors** (first-time) | 14–25% | FEP: 14–19.4% [1,4]; Virtuous first-to-second gift: 25.84% (top: 37.86%) [2]; Fundraising Report Card: 17.88–19.63% [1,7]. ~3/4 new donors give once and leave. |
| **Repeat Donors** | 43–69% | FEP: 69.2% [1], 43.6% YTD [4]; Fundraising Report Card: 53.65% [7]; top monthly: 90% [1]. |
| **Micro Donors** ($1–$100) | 21.3% | FEP Q3 2025 [4]; lowest segment. |
| **Major Donors** ($5K–$50K) | 52% | FEP Q3 2025 [4]; supersize ($50K+): 56.6%. |
| **By Gift Frequency** [4] | Varies | 1-time: 19.2%; 2-time: 38.5%; 3–6 times: 62.5%; 7+: 87.3%. More gifts = higher retention. |
| **Reactivated Donors** | 35.72% | Fundraising Report Card [7]. |

#### Trends and Recommendations
- **Declines Noted**: New donor retention dipped slightly (e.g., 18.1% Q1 2025 [6]); overall stable but below 50% for most.
- **Good Targets**: <40%: Critical; 40–55%: Average (focus here for quick gains); >55%: Strong; top quartile ~70%.
- **Why It Matters**: Retaining donors costs ~$0.20 per $1 raised vs. much higher acquisition costs [3]. Nonprofits exceeding averages often use CRM tools for personalization and recurring gifts [1,2].
- **Data Sources**: Primarily FEP (quarterly scorecard), Virtuous, Fundraising Report Card. Benchmarks from 2024–2026; check latest FEP for Q1 2026 updates.

For your nonprofit, benchmark against similar size/sector (e.g., arts/health vary slightly [1]). Track via: (repeat donors this year / all donors last year) × 100. Aim to beat your prior year by 5–10% annually.
